A still lifted from the finished film, not a photograph and not a phone video, composed as a wide 16:9 reference frame of the whole space with no letterbox bars.

LOCATION PLATE: an ordinary, leafy residential road in a Kent town, seen from the pavement on a quiet weekday morning: a straight road of red-brick semi-detached houses from the 1990s on both sides, each with a small front lawn, a white uPVC porch and a short drive; a wide grass verge between the pavement and the kerb with mature lime trees along it; a few cars parked half on the drives; a postman's red bicycle leaning on a lamp post far down; a low brick wall and a gate in the near foreground. The pavement runs straight away from the camera alongside the verge. Named anchors, all fixed: the straight pavement beside the grass verge and the lime trees; the pairs of red-brick semis with white porches; the low brick wall and gate in the foreground.

Empty: nobody in frame, no person, no product, nothing held, nothing staged, nothing tidied for the photograph.

The set is dressed and layered like a feature production: the top of a low brick front wall and its gate post soft in the near foreground, the empty space in the middle ground, and the room continuing in depth behind them, lived-in, with its own practicals lit. Real surfaces with age and use, and clothes with weave and wear. Nobody stands against a flat wall.

THE LIGHT IS A LIT SET, MOTIVATED BY THE LOW MORNING SUN DOWN THE ROAD THROUGH THE LIME TREES ON FRAME RIGHT. The key is soft, warm low morning sun with dappled shade from the trees, raised slightly above the eye line, at a key-to-fill ratio of about 3:1, so every face has a lit side and a shadow side and the transition between them falls across the near cheek. A fill from the opposite side holds detail in the shadow. A faint edge light from behind separates the head and shoulders from the background. The background is lit only by its own practicals and spill. Every light in frame has a source you could point to.

THE LOOK OF THIS FILM: A British working-class family drama shot like a prestige streaming series — a garden-centre car park, a terraced house with a steep narrow staircase, a GP's consulting room, a builders' yard and a back garden, watched with warmth and restraint. Overcast English daylight and lived-in colour: slate-grey skies, wet tarmac, red brick, khaki and navy workwear and the greens of garden-centre plants; the evenings at home cool blue-grey lit by warm tungsten lamps; warming to low honeyed sun, fresh greens and pale sandstone paving in the After. Highlights roll off softly with a faint warm halation around bulbs and bright windows; clean modern glass with a gentle fall-off toward the frame edges. Captured with natural, neutral colour and a gentle contrast, ungraded — the grade is added later in the edit. Every frame of this film shares exactly this look.

Weight and support everywhere: body load visibly on one foot or braced hand, fabric hanging from contact points and creasing at joints, every object resting on something with a tight contact shadow, soft deforming under hard, liquids level with gravity, nothing floating.

This is a frame from a real film shoot, not a render. Real lens optics: focus falls off gradually either side of one chosen plane, and the out-of-focus areas are soft and round rather than smeared. Highlights behave the way a cinema sensor handles them, rolling off softly into white with a faint warm halation around bulbs and bright windows, never clipping to a hard edge. Shadows hold detail rather than being lifted flat by phone processing. No digital sharpening, no HDR tone-mapping, no phone processing, no beauty retouch, no diffusion glow on skin. Under the grade, skin, fabric and surfaces keep all of their real texture.
